2027-06-04.title: The Most Sacred Heart of Jesus
readings: My heart recoils within me; my compassion grows warm and tender
With joy you will draw water from the wells of salvation
to know the love of Christ that surpasses knowledge
one of the soldiers pierced his side with a spear, and at once blood and water came out
2027-06-04.alt: Solemnity. Year B. Friday after the Second Sunday after Pentecost (in India, the Friday after Corpus Christi). Gloria and Creed. It is the World Day of Prayer for the Sanctification of Priests, and the First Friday of June, the month of the Sacred Heart. Because it is a solemnity, the Friday abstinence does not apply today. Liturgical colour: white.
2027-06-04.verse: Instead, one of the soldiers pierced his side with a spear, and at once blood and water came out.
theo: Today the Church contemplates the love of God made visible in a human heart: the Heart of Jesus, pierced on the Cross. The readings of Year B begin not on Calvary but in the house of a father. Through the prophet Hosea, in the eighth century before Christ, God speaks of Israel as a little child: “When Israel was a child, I loved him, and out of Egypt I called my son.” Then come some of the most tender words in the Old Testament: “Yet it was I who taught Ephraim to walk, I took them up in my arms; but they did not know that I healed them. I led them with cords of human kindness, with bands of love. I was to them like those who lift infants to their cheeks. I bent down to them and fed them.” God is pictured as a parent stooping to a toddler, holding its hands as it learns to walk, lifting it to his cheek. The child grows up and walks away to other gods. Justice would demand punishment. But God's heart does something unexpected: “My heart recoils within me; my compassion grows warm and tender. I will not execute my fierce anger … for I am God and no mortal, the Holy One in your midst, and I will not come in wrath.” The Hebrew says that God's heart is overturned within him, the same word used for the overthrow of Sodom. God's anger is overthrown by his own mercy. God is holy precisely because he does not react like a wounded human being. The responsorial song is from Isaiah: “Surely God is my salvation; I will trust, and will not be afraid … With joy you will draw water from the wells of salvation.” In Latin that verse begins Haurietis aquas, and Pope Pius XII took it as the title of his great encyclical on the Sacred Heart in 1956.

St Paul, in prison, writes to the Ephesians in amazement at his own vocation: “Although I am the very least of all the saints, this grace was given to me to bring to the Gentiles the news of the boundless riches of Christ.” The plan of God, hidden for ages, is now revealed: all peoples are called into one Church. Then Paul kneels: “For this reason I bow my knees before the Father, from whom every family in heaven and on earth takes its name.” His prayer for the Christians of Ephesus is a prayer for us on this feast: “that Christ may dwell in your hearts through faith, as you are being rooted and grounded in love. I pray that you may have the power to comprehend, with all the saints, what is the breadth and length and height and depth, and to know the love of Christ that surpasses knowledge, so that you may be filled with all the fullness of God.” The love of Christ has dimensions. Christians have long seen in them the shape of the Cross: its arms stretched wide to embrace all, its beam reaching down to the lowest and up to heaven. We can never measure that love, but we can know it, the way a child knows its mother's love, by being held in it.

The Gospel takes us to Golgotha on the afternoon of Good Friday. It is the day of Preparation before a great sabbath, and the Law of Moses did not allow a body to remain hanging overnight (Deuteronomy 21:23), so the authorities ask Pilate to have the legs of the crucified broken to hasten their death. The soldiers break the legs of the two others, “But when they came to Jesus and saw that he was already dead, they did not break his legs. Instead, one of the soldiers pierced his side with a spear, and at once blood and water came out.” John, the beloved disciple who stood beneath the Cross with the Mother of Jesus, solemnly insists: “He who saw this has testified so that you also may believe.” He sees two Scriptures fulfilled. “None of his bones shall be broken”: Jesus is the true Passover lamb, whose bones were not to be broken (Exodus 12:46), dying at the hour when the lambs were slaughtered in the Temple. “They will look on the one whom they have pierced” (Zechariah 12:10): the whole world will look at this wound and be drawn to repentance and love. From the opened side flow blood and water. The Fathers saw in them the sacraments of the Church, the water of Baptism and the blood of the Eucharist, and they saw the Church herself born from the side of the new Adam, as Eve was formed from the side of the first Adam while he slept (Catechism 766). This is the Sacred Heart: not a sentimental picture, but the physical heart of the incarnate Son, pierced for us, the sign and the source of the love that Hosea foretold. Jesus said, “learn from me; for I am gentle and humble in heart” (Matthew 11:29). In the visions given to St Margaret Mary Alacoque at Paray-le-Monial (1673–1675), he showed his Heart burning with love and asked for reparation, Holy Communion on the First Fridays, and this feast. Today the Church kneels, as Paul knelt, before the Father, and looks on the one whom we have pierced.
conn: “Out of Egypt I called my son.”
Hosea 11:1 speaks of Israel; Matthew 2:15 sees it fulfilled in the child Jesus returning from Egypt. The Son in whom Israel's story is fulfilled is the one whose Heart we honour today.
“Cords of human kindness.”
God does not drag his people with ropes like oxen but leads them “with bands of love” (Hosea 11:4). Love, not force, is God's way of drawing us.
“My heart recoils within me.”
The Hebrew word for God's heart being overturned is the one used for the overthrow of the cities of the plain (Genesis 19:25). In God, mercy overturns anger.
“The wells of salvation.”

Isaiah 12:3 in Latin reads Haurietis aquas in gaudio de fontibus Salvatoris; Pius XII named his 1956 encyclical on the Sacred Heart from these words. Jesus invites the thirsty to come to him and drink (John 7:37).
“Every family … takes its name.”
In Greek “Father” is pater and “family” is patria: every family on earth reflects the fatherhood of God (Ephesians 3:15).
Breadth, length, height and depth.
Paul's four dimensions of the love of Christ (Ephesians 3:18) have often been read as the shape of the Cross, which embraces the whole world.
“None of his bones shall be broken.”
The law of the Passover lamb (Exodus 12:46; Numbers 9:12). John presents Jesus as the true Lamb, dying at the hour of the Passover sacrifice.
“They will look on the one whom they have pierced.”
Zechariah 12:10, where God promises a spirit of compassion and supplication, so that people mourn over the pierced one as over an only child.
Blood and water.
The Fathers saw in them Baptism and the Eucharist, and the Church born from the side of Christ as Eve from the side of Adam (Catechism 766, 1225).
The feast.

St John Eudes celebrated a liturgical feast of the Heart of Jesus in 1672. After the revelations to St Margaret Mary, Blessed Pius IX extended the feast to the whole Church in 1856, and Leo XIII consecrated the human race to the Sacred Heart in 1899.
altar: At every Mass the pierced Heart of Jesus is opened to us again. The water mixed into the wine at the offertory and the blood of the new covenant on the altar recall what flowed from his side. In the Eucharist we do not receive a memory of his love but the living Heart of Jesus himself, Body and Blood, soul and divinity.

Today the Church prays especially for priests; St John Vianney called the priesthood the love of the Heart of Jesus. Through their hands the sacrifice of Calvary is made present and the waters of salvation are poured out in Baptism and Confession. Pray for the priest who stands at this altar.
outline: Show a picture of the Sacred Heart, the kind that hangs in so many Kerala homes with a small lamp before it, and ask: what is this picture really telling us?
Point 1 · A father teaching his child to walk
In Hosea God bends down, lifts us to his cheek, and his heart recoils from anger.
Isaiah's joy, Paul's prayer: to know the love that surpasses knowledge.
Blood and water: the Lamb, the sacraments, the Church born from his Heart.
Reparation, First Fridays, prayer for priests, and a heart gentle and humble like his.
A soldier's spear, a wound opened, and from it a stream that reaches every baptismal font and every altar in the world.
“They will look on the one whom they have pierced.”
live: If your home has a picture of the Sacred Heart, gather the family before it tonight and renew your consecration; if not, consider enthroning one this month.
Begin, or continue, the nine First Fridays: Mass, Holy Communion and, if possible, confession, in reparation and love.
Today is the World Day of Prayer for the Sanctification of Priests. Pray by name for your parish priest and for the priest who baptised you, and send one of them a word of thanks.
Choose one person who irritates you and treat him or her today with the gentleness and humility of the Heart of Jesus.
fathers: The evangelist chose his word with care: he did not say that the soldier struck or wounded the side, but that he opened it, so that there the door of life might be thrown open, from which flowed the sacraments of the Church, without which no one enters the true life (Tractates on John 120).

The water and the blood are signs of Baptism and of the Holy Mysteries. From these the Church is born. As God formed Eve from the side of the sleeping Adam, so Christ gave us water and blood from his side and built the Church (Baptismal Catecheses 3).
His side was pierced so that through the visible wound we might see the invisible wound of love. Let us enter through the open door into the Heart of Jesus and find rest there (The Mystical Vine).
magis: Jesus knew and loved us each and all during his life, his agony and his Passion, and gave himself up for each one of us; his Sacred Heart, pierced by our sins and for our salvation, is the chief sign and symbol of that love.
The Church is born primarily of Christ's total self-giving for our salvation, signified by the blood and water from the open side of the crucified Jesus.
The prayer of the Church venerates and honours the Heart of Jesus, just as it invokes his most holy name.
The worship of the Sacred Heart is the worship of the love with which God loved us through Jesus, and the practice of our love for God and neighbour.
In the Heart of Christ we find the whole Gospel; from it the Church learns to love the world and to make reparation by building a civilisation of love.
saints: A Visitation nun at Paray-le-Monial in France. Between 1673 and 1675 Jesus showed her his Heart, burning with love and wounded by indifference, and asked for Communion of reparation on the First Fridays, a Holy Hour on Thursday nights, and a feast of his Heart. Her confessor, St Claude La Colombière, a Jesuit, supported her. She was canonised in 1920.

World Day of Prayer for the Sanctification of Priests (today). 5 Jun: the Immaculate Heart of the Blessed Virgin Mary; St Boniface. 6 Jun: Tenth Sunday in Ordinary Time. 9 Jun: St Ephrem. 11 Jun: St Barnabas, apostle.
2027-06-04.prayer: Grant, we pray, almighty God, that we, who glory in the Heart of your beloved Son and recall the wonders of his love for us, may be made worthy to receive an overflowing measure of grace from that fount of heavenly gifts. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who lives and reigns with you in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, for ever and ever. Amen. Let us also pray: Most Sacred Heart of Jesus, pierced for us, we adore you and we trust in you. You taught us to walk and lifted us to your cheek; you bent down and fed us. Forgive our coldness and ingratitude, and accept our love in reparation. Make our hearts like yours, gentle and humble. Bless our homes, our children, and all the priests of your Church. Amen.

quick: Through Hosea God speaks as a parent who taught his child to walk; when Israel turns away, his heart recoils and his compassion grows warm and tender.
Paul prays that Christ may dwell in our hearts and that we may know the love of Christ that surpasses knowledge.
On the Cross a soldier pierces the side of Jesus and blood and water flow out: the Lamb whose bones are not broken, the source of the sacraments and of the Church.
2027-06-04.action: Gather your family before an image of the Sacred Heart tonight and renew your consecration; pray for your priests.
2027-06-04.question: Do I think of God's heart as angry with me, or as Hosea shows it, recoiling from anger and burning with compassion?
catechism: The Sacred Heart: Jesus loved each of us with a human heart.
The Church born from the pierced side of Christ.
Prayer to the Heart of Jesus.
kidsaint: Margaret Mary was a girl in France who was often sick and lonely, and she found her best friend in Jesus in the Blessed Sacrament. She became a sister in a convent. Jesus showed her his Heart, full of love like a fire, and asked her to tell everyone how much he loves them. Many people did not believe her at first, but she kept praying and loving. Because of her we have the feast of the Sacred Heart and the First Fridays. Lesson: Jesus' heart is full of love for you; give him your love in return.
2027-06-04.special: Solemnity of the Most Sacred Heart of Jesus (Year B). Gloria and Creed. World Day of Prayer for the Sanctification of Priests. First Friday of June, the month of the Sacred Heart.
term: Love offered to make up for the coldness, ingratitude and sins by which the love of Christ is wounded. In devotion to the Sacred Heart, reparation means consoling the Lord by our love, especially through Holy Communion received on the First Fridays and the Holy Hour, and repairing the harm of sin by works of justice and charity (Pius XI, Miserentissimus Redemptor, 1928; Pope Francis, Dilexit Nos).

family.explain: God says: I taught you to walk, I held you in my arms, I lifted you to my cheek, I bent down and fed you. That is how much God loves us! And Jesus showed us God's love with his own heart. On the Cross his heart was pierced for us. When we look at the picture of the Sacred Heart in our home, we remember: Jesus loves me with a real human heart, and with all the love of God.
family.intention: We pray for all the priests who have served our family, and for children who are learning to walk and talk.
family.ask: Ask: “Where is the Sacred Heart picture in our home, and how can we pray before it together this month?”

illus: In a hill-country parish in Idukki, an old rubber tapper had kept a lamp burning before a faded picture of the Sacred Heart in his small house for forty years. When the monsoon floods took his house, he lost almost everything. The parish found him a new room, and the first thing he asked for was not a cot but a nail on the wall. A neighbour brought him a new picture. He hung it, lit a small lamp, and said: now this is home. Love that is seen, he said, keeps the heart warm when everything else is wet. (An illustrative story.)

pm.open: Most Sacred Heart of Jesus, we gather before you. Draw us with the cords of human kindness, with bands of love, and teach us to drink with joy from the wells of salvation. Amen.
share: I was to them like those who lift infants to their cheeks (Hosea 11:4). When have I felt God hold me like a child?
To know the love of Christ that surpasses knowledge (Ephesians 3:19). How do I come to know Christ's love: in prayer, in the sacraments, in people?
At once blood and water came out (John 19:34). What does the pierced Heart of Jesus ask of me this month?
pm.resp: With joy you will draw water from the wells of salvation.
interc: For the Church, born from the pierced side of Christ, that she may always proclaim his merciful love.
For priests, on this World Day of Prayer for their sanctification, that they may be men after the Heart of Jesus.
For families consecrated to the Sacred Heart, that their homes may be places of mercy and peace.
For those who feel unloved or have turned away from God, that they may be drawn back with bands of love.
For the sick and dying, that they may rest in the Heart of Jesus.
pm.close: Father, in the Heart of your Son you have shown us the depth of your love. Make our hearts like his, gentle and humble. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, in many of our homes there is a picture of the Sacred Heart of Jesus, with a small lamp burning before it. We have seen it so often that we may not notice it anymore. Today the Church asks us to look at it again, with new eyes, and to understand what it tells us: that God loves us with a heart, and that this Heart was pierced for us.

The first reading shows us God as a father, or a mother, with a little child. It was I who taught Ephraim to walk, I took them up in my arms … I was to them like those who lift infants to their cheeks. I bent down to them and fed them (Hosea 11:3–4). Think of a parent holding a baby's hands as it takes its first steps, or lifting it up to kiss its cheek. That is how God sees you. But the child grows up and runs away. And what does God say? Not, I will destroy you. He says: my heart recoils within me; my compassion grows warm and tender (Hosea 11:8). God's heart is overturned, not against us, but in our favour.

In the second reading St Paul kneels before the Father and prays that we may know the love of Christ that surpasses knowledge (Ephesians 3:19). We cannot measure it. It is broad enough to embrace every person, long enough to last for ever, high enough to lift us to heaven, deep enough to reach the lowest sinner. We cannot measure it, but we can know it, the way a child knows its mother's love, by being held.

Then the Gospel takes us to the Cross. Jesus is already dead. A soldier pierces his side with a spear, and at once blood and water come out (John 19:34). John, who stood there with the Mother of Jesus, says: I saw it, and I tell you so that you may believe. From that wound the Church is born. The water reminds us of our Baptism; the blood, of the Eucharist. Every sacrament we receive flows from the open Heart of Jesus.

This Heart asks something of us. It asks for our love in return. When Jesus showed his Heart to St Margaret Mary, he complained gently that so many people treat his love with coldness and indifference. He asked for reparation: that we console him with our love, receive him in Holy Communion on the First Fridays, and spend time with him in adoration. He also said: learn from me, for I am gentle and humble in heart (Matthew 11:29). Our homes need hearts like that.

Today is also the day of prayer for priests. A priest is a gift from the Heart of Jesus. Pray for your parish priest today. And tonight, gather your family before the picture of the Sacred Heart, light the lamp, and say together: Sacred Heart of Jesus, we trust in you. Let the lamp remind you that his love never goes out. Amen.
kids: Children, have you seen the picture of Jesus pointing to his heart, with a fire and a crown of thorns around it? That is the Sacred Heart. It tells us that Jesus loves us with a real heart, just like ours, but bigger than the whole world! When Jesus died on the cross, a soldier made a hole in his side, and blood and water came out. Jesus gave everything for us.
Today, when you see the Sacred Heart picture at home, stop and say: Jesus, I love you too! And pray for your parish priest, because today is a special day to pray for priests.

intro: Theme: “They will look on the one whom they have pierced.”
The heart of a Father that recoils from anger, the love of Christ that surpasses knowledge, and the pierced side from which the Church is born.

points.h: The heart that recoils from anger
sub: A parent teaching a child to walk.
q: How can I give you up, Ephraim? How can I hand you over, O Israel? … My heart recoils within me; my compassion grows warm and tender.
In this is love, not that we loved God but that he loved us and sent his Son to be the atoning sacrifice for our sins.
points.apply: If you think of God as always angry with you, read Hosea 11 slowly this week and let him lift you to his cheek.

q: With joy you will draw water from the wells of salvation.
Let anyone who is thirsty come to me,
points.apply: Draw from the wells this month: plan a confession and a First Friday Communion, and come to them thirsty.

q: A new heart I will give you, and a new spirit I will put within you; and I will remove from your body the heart of stone and give you a heart of flesh.
and to know the love of Christ that surpasses knowledge, so that you may be filled with all the fullness of God.
points.apply: Pray Paul's prayer (Ephesians 3:14–19) for your family each night this week, using their names.

sub: The Lamb whose bones are not broken.
The Church born from his side.
q: when they look on the one whom they have pierced, they shall mourn for him, as one mourns for an only child,
Instead, one of the soldiers pierced his side with a spear, and at once blood and water came out.
points.apply: Make an act of reparation this week: an hour of adoration, a visit to someone lonely, or a gentle answer where you used to be harsh.

concl: God's heart, Hosea tells us, recoils from anger and burns with compassion; in Jesus that heart became a human heart, and on the Cross it was opened for us.
From the pierced side flow the sacraments and the Church; we answer with love, reparation, prayer for priests, and hearts made gentle and humble like his.
2027-06-04.resolve: Renew your family's consecration to the Sacred Heart this month and keep the First Fridays faithfully.
